findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:1903 snapshots integration before checking receipts, without acquiring the integration lock. template/scripts/delegation_containment.py:452 reads the log without the writer's receipt lock, and :513 consumes every subsequent receipt through EOF. A sibling can therefore advance HEAD before its receipt is appended, or append another advance after the snapshot; classification then sees a missing chain or a chain ending beyond the captured head (:533). Reading during an append can also produce a transient malformed-line error. These cases leave valid Claude execution unrecorded and emit containment friction; retrying after publication settles can succeed.
findings.summary: Concurrent receipt writes can cause a valid sibling advance to be reported as a containment violation.
